Artifacts.Name: KBS Oldowan Choppers & Flakes
Artifacts.Description: Simple river-cobble choppers, polyhedrons, and sharp unretouched flakes used for carcass butchery.

Artifacts.Name: Karari Industry Core Scrapers
Artifacts.Description: Steep-edged core scrapers and heavy-duty stone tools representing a technological transition toward the Acheulean.

Artifacts.Name: Ubeidiya Bifacial Handaxes & Picks
Artifacts.Description: Crude bifacial handaxes and trihedral picks representing one of the earliest Acheulean assemblages outside Africa.

Artifacts.Name: Limestone Spheroids
Artifacts.Description: Faceted spherical stone balls shaped through percussion, likely used for pounding or processing plant and animal tissues.

Artifacts.Name: Dmanisi Pebble Choppers & Flakes
Artifacts.Description: Over 1,000 primitive pebble cores, choppers, and sharp cutting flakes pre-dating Acheulean handaxe technology.

Artifacts.Name: Ternifine Acheulean Handaxes
Artifacts.Description: Large bifacially flaked handaxes recovered directly alongside the Tighennif hominin mandibles.

Artifacts.Name: Broad-Edged Cleavers
Artifacts.Description: Heavy-duty cutting tools with a wide, unretouched transverse bit, characteristic of North African Acheulean industries.

Artifacts.Name: Danakil Basin Acheulean & Mode 1 Tools
Artifacts.Description: Bifacial handaxes and cleavers co-occurring with simpler core-and-flake tools near ancient lacustrine deposits.

Artifacts.Name: Daka Member Early Acheulean Bifaces
Artifacts.Description: Early Acheulean handaxes and cleavers associated with cut-marked bovid and hippopotamus bones.

Artifacts.Name: Quyuanhekou Cobble Tools & Flakes
Artifacts.Description: Heavy-duty choppers, chopping tools, spheroids, and simple flakes manufactured from Han River cobbles.

Artifacts.Name: Gongwangling Pebble Tools & Spheroids
Artifacts.Description: Large unifacial choppers, heavy scrapers, pointed tools, and stone spheroids recovered from loess-paleosol sequences.

Artifacts.Name: Bipolar Vein-Quartz Scrapers & Points
Artifacts.Material: Vein Quartz, Rock Crystal, and Sandstone
Artifacts.Description: Tens of thousands of small retouched scrapers, points, and burins produced primarily using the bipolar anvil technique.

Artifacts.Name: Ash Layers & Burned Bones
Artifacts.Description: Thick accumulations of ash, burned hackberry seeds, and charred animal bones indicating controlled use of fire inside the cave.

Artifacts.Name: Sangiran Flake Industry
Artifacts.Description: Small retouched flakes, side-scrapers, and borers knapped from siliceous river pebbles in the Bapang (Kabuh) formation.

Artifacts.Name: Trinil Engraved Pseudodon Shell
Artifacts.Description: Fossilized mussel shell featuring a deliberate geometric zig-zag engraving—the oldest known abstract engraving—alongside shells modified for cutting.

Artifacts.Name: Olorgesailie Acheulean Handaxe Assemblage
Artifacts.Description: Massive concentrations of finely symmetrical bifacial handaxes and cleavers discovered in ancient Rift Valley lake margins.

Artifacts.Name: Konso Early Acheulean Picks & Handaxes
Artifacts.Description: Some of the earliest known Acheulean large cutting tools, showing the transition from crude unifacial picks to refined bifacial handaxes.

Artifacts.Name: TD6 Mode 1 Flakes & Denticulates
Artifacts.Description: Over 200 simple knapped flakes, notches, and cores used for defleshing animal carcasses and processing cannibalized hominin remains.

Artifacts.Name: Happisburgh Site 3 Flint Cores & Flakes
Artifacts.Description: Around 78 sharp unretouched flint flakes, cores, and flake tools knapped from river-gravel cobbles in a boreal forest environment.
